metadata.name: momo_nft_launchpad
metadata.description: Cookie Chain / Solana fixed-supply NFT drop launchpad with a VRF-free committed reveal

instructions.name: accept_authority
docs: Step 2: the nominee proves control by signing, so governance can never be
handed to an address nobody can use.

instructions.name: buy_nft
docs: Buy the next unit off the curve, minting a fresh NFT.
On a drop with a `graduation_target`, the buy that brings the raise to the target also
graduates the drop (the same effects as `graduate`, `Graduated` emitted after `Bought`).
`max_cost` bounds the price the caller is willing to pay, so a buy that
lands after someone else's cannot silently fill at a worse price.

accounts.name: collection_authority
docs: Writable because Token Metadata's `verify_collection` treats the
collection authority as a potential payer.

accounts.name: collection_master_edition
docs: `verify_collection` touches the collection's edition account.

instructions.name: buy_returned
docs: Buy a unit the pool holds, at the curve price.
The other half of `sell_nft`: a unit sold back goes to the next buyer instead of waiting in
the pool. Same price, fee, allowlist, per-wallet cap and anti-snipe window as `buy_nft`, and
the same graduation at the target. Nothing is minted: the unit moves out of the pool's
custody account, signed by the pool wallet.

accounts.name: nft_metadata
docs: Proof that `nft_mint` is one of this drop's items, as in `SellNft`.

accounts.name: pool_nft_account
docs: The pool's custody account for this item.

instructions.name: cancel_listing
docs: Pull a pool listing off the marketplace (#72).
`pool_wallet` placed the listing and is the only key the venue accepts to withdraw it, and it
signed nothing but `sell`, so a pool listing stood until it sold: it could not be repriced or
withdrawn. That matters because a listing's price is bound to the floor only at the moment of
listing, and the floor rises with every sweep, so a listing placed earlier can end up below
the floor it was meant to respect.
The stock Auction House `cancel`, signed by the pool wallet: it revokes the venue's delegate on
the pool's token account and closes the trade state. The unit never left the pool (a delegate
listing is not an escrow), so it is immediately listable again. Gated like
`list_on_marketplace` on WHO (the creator or the operator, a graduated drop), but not on WHERE:
- Any house the venue program owns is accepted, not only the pinned one. A listing the live
build placed on some other house has to be removable too, and a cancel signed by the pool
wallet can only take away the pool's own approval and refund rent to `pool_wallet`. The
house's terms (fee, flags) do not matter for that, so they are not checked.
- Not gated by `paused`, so an incident can still pull open listings.
- Not gated on collection membership either, unlike listing. Any approval the pool wallet
holds has to be revocable, including one on a unit that is not this drop's (a listing the
live build placed before membership was checked), and removing it can only help.
Which listing is being cancelled is decided by the unit's listing record, never by the
caller's `price` alone (review of #83). A wrong price used to fall into the "already gone"
branch below, revoke the approval and report a cancel while the real trade state stayed open;
the next listing then re-approved the venue and brought the stale listing back, below the
floor. Now:
- With a record (every listing this program places): `price` must equal the recorded price
and `seller_trade_state` the recorded trade state. If that trade state is gone, the listing
ended on the venue's side (its authority cancelled it, or the unit sold), so any leftover
approval is revoked here. If it is open, the venue's `cancel` closes it. Either way the
record is closed and its rent returned to the signer. This is also how a record whose unit
sold on the venue (`pool_nft_account.amount == 0`) is cleared.
- Without a record (a listing placed before records existed, or on another house): only the
venue's own `cancel` is used, so the trade state must exist and the venue checks that it is
this unit's listing at `price`. Nothing is revoked on the caller's word.
The trade state's rent goes back to `pool_wallet` (the venue refunds the wallet that signs),
where `sweep_pool_proceeds` will move it onto the floor.

accounts.name: signer
docs: The creator or the protocol operator, checked in the handler exactly as for listing. `mut`
because it receives the listing record's rent when the record is closed.

accounts.name: pool_nft_account
docs: The pool's custody account for the listed unit: the venue revokes its delegate here.

accounts.name: pool_wallet
docs: signed the listing, and receives the trade state's rent back.

accounts.name: listing
docs: placed the listing, and is empty for a listing placed before records existed; the handler
reads it only when this program owns it, and closes it when it does.

accounts.name: auction_house
docs: only the pinned one: see `cancel_listing`.

accounts.name: seller_trade_state
docs: With a listing record it must be the recorded one: the trade state the venue accepted for the
recorded price, open or already gone. Without a record it must be open, and Auction House
re-derives it from the wallet, house, token account, mint and `price` before closing it.

instructions.name: claim_creator_proceeds
docs: Sweep the creator side to the creator and their royalty partner, in one
transaction, split by the share fixed at launch. Pull, not push: pushing
on every trade would spend a trader's compute to dust two wallets.

accounts.name: partner_payment_account
docs: Required only when the drop has a royalty partner with a non-zero share.

instructions.name: close_collection
docs: Mark a drop that never sold out as ended, once its window has closed.
Anyone may close a drop that FAILED — window over, not sold out — because `Ended` is the only
way into `redeem_wind_down`, and that refund is supposed to need nobody's cooperation. When
this required the creator or operator, holders of a failed drop still depended on exactly
the person the wind-down exists to route around.
A SOLD-OUT drop is the opposite case: it is waiting to graduate, and closing it would push
holders onto the wind-down instead of the floor they bought into. So once `minted` reaches
`total_supply` it stays creator/operator-only, as before. Without that bound anyone could end
a successful drop the moment its window closed. A drop whose raise has reached its
`graduation_target` is successful in the same way, and gets the same bound.

accounts.name: signer
docs: Anyone, for a drop that failed; the creator or operator for one that sold out. Checked in
the handler.

instructions.name: create_collection
docs: Create a drop: mints the collection NFT, writes its metadata and master
edition, seals the fairness commitment and fixes the curve.

instructions.name: emergency_pause
docs: The hot operator may FREEZE trading instantly in an incident, but only
governance can unfreeze — so a compromised operator costs availability,
never funds.

instructions.name: graduate
docs: Graduate a drop that sold out, or that reached its `graduation_target`.
Locks the creator-chosen slice of the raise as the permanent floor —
irrevocable, with no instruction anywhere that can withdraw it — and
moves the remainder to the creator. From here the collection trades on
the marketplace, with the floor standing behind it forever, and selling
back to the curve is closed. Supply not yet minted (a target graduation)
keeps minting on the same curve, at random, through `request_mint`.
Permissionless either way. A drop with no target (every drop created
before targets existed) graduates exactly as before: at sell-out only,
with the same error otherwise. A drop WITH a target graduates inside the
`buy_nft` that reaches it, so for those this is only a fallback: called
on a drop that already graduated it fails with `InvalidCollectionState`
and changes nothing.

accounts.name: signer
docs: Permissionless: graduation is a fact about the drop, not a privilege.

instructions.name: init_vaults
docs: Create the drop's three vaults.
Permissionless and idempotent, and deliberately NOT folded into
`create_collection`: that instruction already creates a mint, a token
account, a metadata account and a master edition. Three more account
creations would push it past the transaction size limit.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Anyone may pay the rent; the accounts are PDAs with fixed seeds, so a
griefer can only pre-pay for us.

instructions.name: list_on_marketplace
docs: List one pool-held NFT on Baked Bazaar at the graduation price.
One listing per transaction, called repeatedly after graduation — a batch
would not fit the size limit. The pool is the seller: the collection PDA
owns the token account and signs the CPI itself.
Auction House `sell` is a DELEGATE listing, not an escrow: the NFT stays
in the pool's account until someone executes the sale, so listing can
never strand an item somewhere we cannot recover it.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Pays the trade-state rent, and must be the creator or the protocol operator — checked in the
handler. This was permissionless on the theory that listing at the graduation price is a
published outcome rather than a privilege, but `price` is a caller argument, so anyone could
list every pool-held item at one base unit and execute the sale against themselves.

accounts.name: pool_nft_account
docs: The pool's custody account for this item; the pool_wallet PDA owns it.

accounts.name: pool_wallet
docs: accounts and is the only account here the System program is allowed to debit.

accounts.name: listing
docs: The unit's listing record, written once the venue accepts the listing; the payer covers its
rent, which comes back on `cancel_listing`. An existing record means the unit is already
listed, and the listing is refused (see the handler).

accounts.name: nft_metadata
docs: Proof that the unit is one of THIS drop's, through the same `is_collection_item` check
`sell_nft` and the redeem paths use. Anyone can send a token to `pool_wallet`, and listing
used to take whatever the pool held: a forged NFT dropped there would go on sale under the
pool's signature, with royalties paid to whoever its metadata names. Decoded as Token
Metadata, owner-checked, and pinned to the mint by its PDA seeds, so no other unit's
metadata can stand in for it.

accounts.name: auction_house
docs: `venue_fee_for_listing`. Auction House then validates the authority and fee account against
it.

instructions.name: nominate_authority
docs: Step 1 of the two-step handoff. Nominating is reversible; the successor is
not authority until it signs `accept_authority`.

instructions.name: redeem_floor
docs: Redeem an NFT against the permanent floor, after graduation.
Pays `floor_reserve / floor_redeemable` and BURNS the unit. The floor price is invariant
under redemption (see `logic::floor_price`), so this cannot be drained into a falling floor:
the last holder gets the same price as the first.
That invariant needs one slot per unit that exists, and the burn is what keeps it (#76). The
unit used to move into pool custody instead, where `list_on_marketplace` could sell it again
with its slot already spent: every resale put one more holder outside the pool against the
same `floor_redeemable`, so the last holders out found the reserve gone. Burned, a redeemed
unit cannot be listed, sold or redeemed again, and `floor_redeemable` stays equal to the
number of units still in existence. Pool inventory that CAN be listed is only what holders
sold back into the curve before graduation, and each of those units still owns its slot.

accounts.name: nft_mint
docs: `mut` because the unit is burned, which lowers the mint's supply.

accounts.name: nft_metadata
docs: The same proof `sell_nft` requires, through the same helper. The floor is the thing this
program promises hardest, and it was the cheaper of the two to empty: `floor_redeemable`
starts at `total_supply`, so junk mints could redeem the whole reserve in one pass and leave
every real holder with `NothingToClaim`.

instructions.name: redeem_wind_down
docs: Take your share of the raise back out of a drop that never sold out.
`end_ts` passing without a sell-out used to be the end of the story, and the end of the
money with it: `sell_nft` reverts past `end_ts`, `graduate` requires
`minted == total_supply` so it can never run on a drop that fell short, and
`close_collection` only moves the state to the terminal `Ended`. From `Ended`, no instruction
in this program could move anything out of `payment_vault` — the whole raise was locked for
good and every holder was left with an unsellable NFT and no refund. A drop that sells slowly
is the LIKELY outcome for most launches, so that was the common path, not an edge case.
The price is `payment_raised_net / circulating`, which is `redeem_floor`'s shape and holds
`redeem_floor`'s invariant. Writing `R = qC + r`, paying `q` leaves `R' = q(C-1) + r` over
`C' = C - 1`, so the next quotient is `q + r/(C-1)` — never less than `q`. The last holder
out cannot be paid less than the first, so there is no race to the exit and no advantage in
being early.
Permissionless, and it has to be: a creator whose drop failed is the last person whose
cooperation the holders should need. It shares `RedeemFloor`'s accounts deliberately, so the
collection-membership check is literally the same one and cannot drift.

accounts.name: nft_mint
docs: `mut` because the unit is burned, which lowers the mint's supply.

accounts.name: nft_metadata
docs: The same proof `sell_nft` requires, through the same helper. The floor is the thing this
program promises hardest, and it was the cheaper of the two to empty: `floor_redeemable`
starts at `total_supply`, so junk mints could redeem the whole reserve in one pass and leave
every real holder with `NothingToClaim`.

instructions.name: refund_mint
docs: Return a request's payment in full, when it can no longer settle. Permissionless, never
paused, and the money can only go to the buyer.
One case only, for the oldest pending request (resolution is strictly in order): its
randomness slot has left `SlotHashes` (about 512 slots, ~4 minutes) without a settle. A
refund, not a new slot: re-rolling would hand a free second draw to whoever let the first one
lapse, and a refund is the one outcome that cannot strand the money.
There used to be a second case, a request priced under a floor that had risen since. It let a
buyer who had seen a bad draw cancel it, by lifting the floor with a dust donation and a sweep
in the same transaction (#92 review). Sweeps now wait for the queue to drain, nothing else
can lift the floor over a pending price, and a settle never fails on the floor, so that case
is gone.
The curve steps back one unit, so the price the next buyer pays is as if the request had never
been made (or higher, never lower). The buyer's payment-mint ATA is created if it is missing,
paid by the caller, so a buyer who closed their account cannot hold up the queue.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Anyone. Pays for the buyer's payment ATA only if the buyer has none.

accounts.name: collection
docs: `mut` for `mint_requests_pending`.

accounts.name: buyer
docs: of the request back.

accounts.name: minter
docs: The refunded unit no longer counts against the buyer's wallet cap.

accounts.name: buyer_payment_account
docs: Any payment-mint token account the buyer owns: the refund can only go to the buyer. If the
buyer has none, anyone can create their ATA first (the ATA program's permissionless
`CreateIdempotent`, in the same transaction), so a buyer cannot hold up the queue by closing
their accounts.

instructions.name: request_mint
docs: Reserve a post-graduation mint at the curve's current price.
The price is taken now, the curve moves on by one unit now (so concurrent buyers each get the
next price, exactly as sequential buys would), and the payment (price plus fee) is held in
`payment_vault` as escrow until the request settles or is refunded. The item is drawn later,
from the hash of slot `now + RANDOMNESS_DELAY_SLOTS`, which nobody can know yet.
The buyer also deposits the rent of the item's four accounts (and Token Metadata's fee), as a
`buy_nft` buyer pays them, so whoever settles is repaid and the buyer gets the rest back.
One open request per buyer per drop. The first request after graduation opens the queue and
pays its rent.

accounts.name: collection
docs: `mut` for `mint_requests_pending`.

accounts.name: mint_queue
docs: Opened by the first request after graduation, which pays its rent. Its size depends only on
`total_supply`, so every later request passes the same `space` check.

accounts.name: request
docs: `init`, not `init_if_needed`: a buyer with a pending request must wait for it to resolve.

accounts.name: payment_vault
docs: Holds the escrow until the request resolves, ring-fenced by `mint_queue.escrowed`.

instructions.name: reveal
docs: Publish the shuffle seed.
Deliberately NOT verified on-chain: the commitment covers
`sha256(seed ‖ ordered_uris)` and the URI list lives off-chain, so the
check is permissionless and external. A creator who publishes a seed that
does not reproduce the commitment is caught by every observer at once.

instructions.name: sell_nft
docs: Sell a unit back into the curve.
The NFT moves into the pool's inventory and the seller is paid the curve
price less the fee. This is the guaranteed exit: it works from the first
block, at a price anyone can compute in advance.

accounts.name: token_metadata_program
docs: Declared BEFORE `nft_metadata`: Anchor resolves accounts in declaration order, so a
constraint can only name an account above it.

accounts.name: nft_metadata
docs: Proof that `nft_mint` is one of this drop's items — see `is_collection_item`. Pinned to the
mint by its own PDA seeds, so no other item's metadata can be passed in its place.

accounts.name: pool_nft_account
docs: The pool's custody account for this item.

accounts.name: pool_wallet
docs: accounts and is the only account here the System program is allowed to debit.

instructions.name: set_graduation_target
docs: Let the drop graduate once its raise reaches `graduation_target`, without selling out; the
rest of the supply then keeps minting on the curve, at random (see `request_mint`). 0 clears
it: graduate at sell-out only, as every drop did before.
Creator only, and only while the drop is `Created`, i.e. before its first unit: the target is
part of what a buyer buys into, so it is fixed from the first mint on. Its own instruction
rather than a `CollectionParams` field, so `create_collection`'s instruction data, which the
backend already builds, does not change; send it in the same transaction as `init_vaults`,
which no buy can precede.
Bounded to between half and all of the raise at sell-out under this drop's own curve
(`logic::sellout_raise`), computed here from the curve the drop was created with. Below half,
graduation would lock a floor from too little of the raise; above all of it, the target could
be unreachable.

instructions.name: set_platform_royalty
docs: Set the platform's marketplace royalty for drops created from now on. A drop fixes it at
create, so this never changes the creators of an item already minted, nor of a live drop.
The wallet must be a plain system-owned wallet: on Baked Bazaar's native house a royalty is
paid in lamports straight to the creator address, and a token account would strand it. It
must also hold at least the rent-exempt minimum: Auction House silently SKIPS a native
royalty payout that would leave the payee below it, and the seller keeps the cut. This only
holds at the moment of the call, so the wallet must never be drained below that minimum.
`royalty_bps` 0 turns the royalty off for new drops.

instructions.name: settle_mint
docs: Draw and mint the oldest pending request. Permissionless: the backend keeper calls it about a
second after the request, but anyone may, and the outcome is the same whoever does.
Needs the request's randomness slot to be in `SlotHashes` (see `logic::find_slot_hash`). The
draw is `draw_value(slot_hash, collection, request, nonce) mod remaining`, rank-selected over
the indices not yet minted. The caller passes the `index` that draw gives (it is a pure
function of public state, so the keeper computes it) because the item's mint is the PDA
`["item", collection, index]` and Anchor creates it before this handler runs; a wrong index is
refused, and the PDA means no index can ever be minted twice.
The item is the same as a `buy_nft` item: immutable metadata at `{base_uri}{index}.json`,
verified into the collection, a master edition with max supply 0, the drop's creators. The
escrow splits as `logic::post_grad_split` says: the fee to the platform and creator vaults as
on any trade, at least the floor per unit onto the floor (with one more slot), the rest to the
creator. The caller pays the item's rent and is repaid from the buyer's deposit.
Nothing about the floor can make this fail: once the randomness exists, the head request
settles, and its only other exit is the expiry refund. Nobody, the buyer included, gets to
choose between the two after seeing the draw.

accounts.name: settler
docs: Anyone. Pays the item's rent and is repaid from the request's deposit.

accounts.name: buyer
docs: the unspent part of the deposit.

accounts.name: nft_mint
docs: The drawn item's mint, at the index's PDA. Created here, so an index already minted fails.

instructions.name: sweep_platform_fees
docs: Sweep the platform's cut. Operator-signed, destination pinned to Config —
the operator chooses WHEN, never WHERE.

accounts.name: treasury_payment
docs: Destination pinned to Config: the operator picks when, never where.

instructions.name: sweep_pool_proceeds
docs: Bring marketplace proceeds back into the reserve that backs the floor.
Auction House pays the SELLER WALLET, and the seller wallet here is `pool_wallet` — the
dataless PDA that holds the pool's inventory. Before this, `pool_wallet` signed only the
marketplace CPIs (`sell`, and since #72 `cancel`), neither of which moves money out, so every
unit the pool sold on the marketplace left its payment somewhere no instruction in this
program could move. The listing path was shipping money into a hole.
WHERE the money lands depends on the auction house's treasury mint, and the production one
is the case that matters. Baked Bazaar's auction house has `treasury_mint = So111…112`, the
same as our `payment_mint`, and on that native path `execute_sale` asserts the seller's
payment receipt account IS the seller and pays LAMPORTS straight to `pool_wallet` — never to
its wCOOK token account. An earlier version read only the token account, so against
production it always found nothing and the proceeds stayed stuck. Both paths are swept:
- native: every lamport on `pool_wallet` above its rent-exempt minimum moves into
`payment_vault` and is wrapped there with SyncNative. The minimum stays, because the next
`list_on_marketplace` relies on the pool holding exactly that before it tops up the rent.
- SPL: for an auction house whose treasury is a token, the pool's token account, when one
is passed.
Lamports above the minimum can include trade-state rent Auction House refunds to the seller
when a listing settles or is cancelled — rent the listing's payer originally covered. It is swept too: this
instruction can only move money toward holders, and a floor slightly higher than earned is
the conservative error.
The proceeds go onto `floor_reserve`, which raises the floor for every unit still
outstanding. Permissionless for the same reason: the only thing this can do is pay holders.
Refused while any post-graduation mint request is pending (#92 review). A request's price is
fixed when it is made, and its draw becomes public a few slots before anyone settles it; if
the floor could still move in between, raising it past the price is a way to cancel a draw
you have already seen. With sweeps held back, nothing in that window can lift the floor over
a pending price (proof at `logic::post_grad_price`). Proceeds simply wait in `pool_wallet`
until the queue drains, which takes seconds (or one expiry). Also refused while no unit
exists: there is nobody to credit, and a reserve with no unit would be handed whole to the
next mint.

accounts.name: signer
docs: Anyone. The instruction can only move money toward holders.

accounts.name: pool_wallet
docs: accounts, and Auction House pays the seller wallet, which is this. `mut` because on the
native path the proceeds ARE its lamports.

accounts.name: pool_payment_account
docs: Where an SPL-treasury auction house leaves the money. Optional: on the native path — Baked
Bazaar's — this account usually does not exist, and requiring it made the sweep uncallable.

fields.name: index
docs: Sequential position, and the number in `{base_uri}{index}.json`.

fields.name: cost
docs: Curve price paid, before the fee.

types.name: BoughtReturned
docs: A unit the pool held was bought off the curve. No `index`: the program does not track which
index a returned unit has (it is in the unit's metadata).

fields.name: cost
docs: Curve price paid, before the fee.

types.name: Collection
docs: One drop. Seeds: `["collection", collection_mint]`.
Keyed on the collection mint (not a counter) for the same reason the pool PDA
is keyed on its token mint: the mint is the natural, collision-free identity,
and any client can derive the account from the thing it already knows.

fields.name: royalty_partner
docs: Optional second payee who shares the creator's cut, on curve fees AND on
marketplace royalties. Zero = no partner.

fields.name: collection_mint
docs: The collection NFT itself. Every minted item is verified into it.

fields.name: virtual_payment_reserve
docs: Constant-product virtual reserves. `x = virtual_payment_reserve +
payment_raised_net`, `y = virtual_nft_reserve - circulating`.

fields.name: payment_raised_net
docs: Payment side of the curve: what buyers put in, less what sellers took out.

fields.name: total_supply
docs: Fixed supply. `minted` never exceeds it.

fields.name: minted
docs: Units ever minted.

fields.name: inventory
docs: Units the pool bought back and holds. `circulating = minted - inventory - burned`.

fields.name: max_per_wallet
docs: 0 = unlimited.

fields.name: allowlist_root
docs: Allowlist phase: early ACCESS, not a discount (the curve sets the price).
Zero root = public from `launch_ts`.

fields.name: floor_lock_bps
docs: Share of the raise locked forever at graduation to back the floor.
Creator-chosen at launch, bounded by `config.max_floor_lock_bps`.

fields.name: floor_reserve
docs: Locked payment backing the floor. Only leaves via `redeem_floor`.

fields.name: floor_redeemable
docs: Units still redeemable against the floor. `floor_reserve / floor_redeemable`
is the floor price, and it is invariant under redemption. Equal to the
number of units that still exist (`minted - burned`) for the whole
graduated life of a drop, because a redeemed unit is burned in the same
instruction that takes its slot, and a unit minted after graduation adds
its slot in the instruction that mints it (`settle_mint`).

fields.name: commitment
docs: `sha256(seed ‖ ordered_uris)`, fixed BEFORE the first mint. The
position-to-artwork mapping is sealed here, so nobody — us included — can
favour a wallet after minting starts.

fields.name: reveal_seed
docs: Published at reveal so anyone can recompute the commitment and check it.

fields.name: seller_fee_bps
docs: Royalty written immutably into every item: the creator's own royalty plus the platform's
(see `platform_royalty_pct`), split creator/partner/platform. The total, because the total is
what Auction House takes off a sale.

fields.name: partner_share_bps
docs: Partner's share OF the creator side. 0 = creator takes all.

fields.name: collection_authority_bump
docs: PDA holding update authority over the COLLECTION NFT so the program can
verify items into it. Grants no power over item metadata, which is
created immutable.

fields.name: burned
docs: Units burned on the way out: by `redeem_floor` after graduation, by `redeem_wind_down` after
a failed drop. A burned unit has used its floor slot and no longer exists, so it can never be
listed or redeemed again (#76). Taken from the padding, so accounts written by an older
binary read it as zero, which is correct for them.

fields.name: platform_royalty_wallet
docs: The platform's royalty payee and its whole-percent share of `seller_fee_bps`, fixed from
`Config` at create so every item of a drop carries the same creators. Taken from the padding,
so a drop created by an older binary reads as no platform royalty, which is what its items
carry.

fields.name: graduation_target
docs: Creator-chosen graduation target, in the units of `payment_raised_net`: the drop may graduate
once its raise reaches this, without selling out, and the rest of the supply then mints on the
curve at random (see `request_mint`). Bounded at `set_graduation_target` to between half and
all of the raise at sell-out under this drop's own curve. 0 = graduate at sell-out only, which
is what every drop created before this field existed reads, from the padding.

fields.name: graduation_raise
docs: `payment_raised_net` at the moment of graduation: the curve's payment side, which
`payment_raised_net` itself no longer carries once `graduate` zeroes it. Post-graduation
minting prices off the curve from this point. Written by every graduation from this binary on;
zero (from the padding) on a drop graduated earlier, which sold out and has nothing to mint.

fields.name: mint_requests_pending
docs: Post-graduation mint requests not yet settled or refunded: the drop's `MintQueue` pending
count, kept here too so `sweep_pool_proceeds` can refuse while any is pending without taking
the queue account (its accounts stay as the backend builds them). Moves in lockstep with the
queue: +1 in `request_mint`, -1 in `settle_mint` and `refund_mint`.

fields.name: padding
docs: Append new fixed-size fields HERE. Strings stay last.

fields.name: commitment
docs: The fairness commitment, recorded at the moment it was sealed.

fields.name: floor_lock_bps
docs: The creator's trust signal: how much of the raise will be locked as the
permanent floor at graduation.

fields.name: platform_royalty_wallet
docs: The platform's royalty payee and its whole-percent share of `seller_fee_bps`, which is the
total (creator + platform). Default / 0 when the drop carries no platform royalty.

fields.name: base_uri
docs: Base for each item's final URI: `{base_uri}{index}.json`.

fields.name: collection_uri
docs: The collection-level JSON (not an item).

fields.name: virtual_payment_reserve
docs: Curve shape. `virtual_nft_reserve` must exceed `total_supply`.

fields.name: commitment
docs: `sha256(seed ‖ ordered_uris)`. Must be non-zero.

fields.name: royalty_partner
docs: Optional second payee sharing the creator's cut. Zero = none.

fields.name: floor_lock_bps
docs: Share of the raise locked forever as the floor. The creator's trust
signal: higher means buyers have a stronger guaranteed exit.

types.name: CollectionState
docs: Lifecycle of a drop.

types.name: Config
docs: Protocol singleton. Seeds: `["config"]`.

fields.name: authority
docs: Governance. Intended to sit behind the cold multisig.

fields.name: pending_authority
docs: Two-step rotation target. Zero means no handoff in flight; the successor
must sign `accept_authority`, so governance can never be handed to an
address that cannot use it.

fields.name: operator
docs: Hot key for automated, non-custodial ops (pause, sweep, list). Separated
from `authority` from day one rather than retrofitted.

fields.name: payment_mint
docs: The mint every drop trades in (wCOOK).

fields.name: treasury_payment
docs: Where the platform's cut is swept to.

fields.name: trade_fee_bps
docs: Fee on EVERY curve trade, buy and sell alike. 300 = 3%.

fields.name: platform_share_bps
docs: Share OF `trade_fee_bps` kept by the platform; the remainder is the
creator side. 5000 = half, i.e. 1.5% platform / 1.5% creator at a 3% fee.

fields.name: default_seller_fee_bps
docs: Royalty policy. Kept as config rather than a constant so it can be
retuned without a redeploy. Both bound the CREATOR's own royalty; the
platform royalty goes on top, and `max + platform_royalty_bps` must fit
`ROYALTY_HARD_CAP_BPS`.

fields.name: max_floor_lock_bps
docs: Ceiling on how much of a raise a creator may lock as the permanent floor.

fields.name: paused
docs: Freezes new trades. Only governance can unpause.

fields.name: platform_royalty_wallet
docs: The platform's marketplace royalty, written into the metadata of drops created from now on
as an extra creator on top of the creator's own royalty. The curve fee ends at graduation;
this is how the platform earns on secondary sales. A plain wallet, not a token account:
Auction House pays a native-mint royalty in lamports straight to the creator address. Zero
wallet or zero bps = off. Taken from the padding, so the live account reads it as off.

fields.name: padding
docs: Append new fields HERE, shrinking the padding. Never mid-struct.

fields.name: trade_fee_bps
docs: Fee on every curve trade. 300 = 3%.

fields.name: platform_share_bps
docs: Platform's share of that fee. 5000 = half.

fields.name: floor_reserve
docs: Locked forever. No instruction can withdraw it.

fields.name: floor_price
docs: What every holder can always redeem for.

fields.name: inventory
docs: Units the pool holds, to be listed on the marketplace.

types.name: GraduationTargetSet
docs: The creator set (or cleared, with 0) the raise at which the drop may graduate early.

fields.name: sellout_raise
docs: The raise at sell-out under this drop's curve, which the target was bounded against.

types.name: Listed
docs: A pool-held unit was listed on the marketplace after graduation.

types.name: Listing
docs: One open pool listing on the marketplace. Seeds: `["listing", collection, nft_mint]`.
Written by `list_on_marketplace` (the lister pays the rent) and closed by `cancel_listing`. It is
what lets a cancel tell "the venue already closed this listing" from "the caller named a price
that was never listed": the record holds the exact trade state the listing created, so a cancel
can only ever act on that one (review of #83).

fields.name: price
docs: The listed price, in payment-mint base units.

fields.name: trade_state
docs: The venue's trade state for this listing, as the venue derived and accepted it.

types.name: ListingCancelled
docs: A pool listing was pulled off the marketplace. The unit stays in pool custody, listable again.

types.name: MintQueue
docs: The post-graduation mint of one drop: the curve position it prices from, the FIFO queue of
requests, the payment they escrow, and which indices have been minted. Seeds:
`["mint_queue", collection]`.
A separate account, not more `Collection` fields: the minted-index bitmap is up to 1,256 bytes,
and `Collection` is a fixed 713 bytes on chain that cannot grow without a realloc of every live
drop. Opened by the first `request_mint` after graduation (that buyer pays its rent), so neither
`graduate`'s accounts nor a legacy drop change at all.

fields.name: base
docs: `minted` when the queue opened, i.e. at graduation: every index below it was minted before
graduation, in order. Kept for indexers; the bitmap is the source of truth.

fields.name: curve_raised
docs: The curve's position for post-graduation pricing, `x = virtual_payment_reserve +
curve_raised`, `y = virtual_nft_reserve - curve_circulating`. Starts where the curve stood at
graduation and moves forward one unit per request (back one per refund). Redemptions and
marketplace sales do not move it, so the price only ever continues up the same curve.

fields.name: next_nonce
docs: Nonce the next request gets.

fields.name: settle_cursor
docs: Nonce of the oldest request not yet settled or refunded. Requests are resolved strictly in
nonce order, so `next_nonce - settle_cursor` are pending.

fields.name: escrowed
docs: Payment (price + fee) that pending requests hold inside `payment_vault`. The vault always
holds at least `floor_reserve + escrowed` after graduation.

fields.name: lock_bound
docs: The largest floor share (`floor_lock_bps` of the price) of any request made since the queue
was last empty. `request_mint` prices no lower than this while requests are pending, because
an earlier request's settle can lift the floor to its share (see `logic::post_grad_price`).

fields.name: padding
docs: Append new fixed-size fields HERE. The bitmap stays last.

fields.name: minted_bits
docs: One bit per index of the supply, set once it is minted (or does not exist: bits past
`total_supply` in the last word are set at open). The draw picks among the clear bits.

types.name: MintRefunded
docs: A post-graduation request was refunded in full: its randomness expired, or the floor rose
above its price before it could settle.

fields.name: amount
docs: Price plus fee, returned. A refund is always an expiry: the randomness slot left
`SlotHashes` before anyone settled.

types.name: MintRequest
docs: One buyer's pending post-graduation mint. Seeds: `["mint_request", collection, buyer]`, so a
buyer has at most one at a time. Created by `request_mint`, closed by `settle_mint` or
`refund_mint`.

fields.name: nonce
docs: Position in the drop's queue. Also an input of the draw.

fields.name: target_slot
docs: The slot whose hash decides the item: the first produced slot at or after this one.

fields.name: cost
docs: Price paid, before the fee: the net that `settle_mint` splits between floor and creator.

fields.name: fee_platform
docs: The fee, split as it was at request time, so a later config change cannot reprice it.

fields.name: rent_deposit
docs: Lamports the buyer put up, on top of this account's own rent, for the item's four accounts
(mint, token account, metadata, master edition). Whoever settles pays those and is repaid
from this; the rest goes back to the buyer.

types.name: MintRequested
docs: A buyer reserved a post-graduation mint. The item is drawn when it settles.

fields.name: nonce
docs: Queue position: requests settle in this order.

fields.name: target_slot
docs: The draw uses the hash of the first produced slot at or after this one.

fields.name: cost
docs: Price paid into escrow, before the fee.

fields.name: curve_circulating
docs: The curve's position after this request: what the next request is priced from.

types.name: MintSettled
docs: A post-graduation request was drawn and minted.

fields.name: index
docs: The drawn index: the number in `{base_uri}{index}.json`.

fields.name: slot
docs: The slot whose hash decided the draw.

fields.name: to_floor
docs: The part of `cost` that went onto the floor, and the part that went to the creator side.

types.name: Minter
docs: Per-wallet trade record for one drop. Seeds: `["minter", collection, owner]`.
Exists so `max_per_wallet` and the opening-window throttle are enforced
on-chain rather than trusted from the client.

types.name: PoolProceedsSwept
docs: Marketplace proceeds were brought back out of the pool wallet and onto the floor.

fields.name: proceeds
docs: What the seller actually received, after the fee.

types.name: WindDownRedeemed
docs: A holder of a drop that never sold out took their share of the raise back.

fields.name: payment_raised_net
docs: What is left in the raise, and how many units are still out, after this one.
